name: Secondary Vasculitis Associated with Malignancy

criteria.description: Confirmed diagnosis of an underlying malignancy
Clinical evidence of vasculitis affecting one or more organ systems
Exclusion of primary vasculitis and other secondary causes
Histopathologic confirmation of vasculitis in affected tissue
Improvement of vasculitis symptoms following treatment of malignancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of underlying malignancy with clinical vasculitis and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and supported by histopathology and response to cancer therapy

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic skin lesions such as palpable purpura and ulcers
searchTerms: skin blood vessel inflammation with tissue death

pathognomonic.notes: Fever, weight loss, and malaise associated with paraneoplastic syndrome
searchTerms: general symptoms like fatigue and weight loss

common.notes: Mononeuritis multiplex or polyneuropathy due to vessel inflammation
Joint pain or inflammation without erosive changes
Cough, hemoptysis, or dyspnea from pulmonary vasculitis

occasional.notes: Scleritis or uveitis secondary to vasculitis
Abdominal pain or bleeding due to mesenteric vessel involvement
Due to vascular leakage or renal dysfunction
Enlarged lymph nodes related to malignancy or inflammation

rare.notes: Stroke or encephalopathy due to cerebral vessel involvement

laboratory: Possible presence of circulating immune complexes
imaging: Angiographic evidence of vessel irregularities or stenosis
CT or MRI showing organ ischemia or infarction
other: Histopathology showing leukocytoclastic or necrotizing vasculitis
Improvement of vasculitis with treatment of underlying malignancy

distinguishingFeatures: Different clinical course and treatment response

redFlags: Rapid progression of vasculitic symptoms despite immunosuppression
New onset of vasculitis symptoms in a patient with known malignancy
Signs of multi-organ failure or ischemia
references: Jennette JC, Falk RJ. Vasculitis associated with malignancy. Rheum Dis Clin North Am. 1990;16(3):573-588.
Guillevin L, Mahr A, Callard P, et al. Vasculitis and malignancy: a study of 26 cases. Medicine (Baltimore). 2001;80(1):17-28.
Sunderkötter C, Sindrilaru A. Paraneoplastic vasculitis. Clin Dermatol. 2014;32(4):507-512.
